subject: Lumenix model shortlist & loadshape / token estimates — handoff
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Holt <sara@lumenix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Lumenix model shortlist & loadshape / token estimates — initial pass

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I pulled together a concise model shortlist and a first-pass loadshape + token estimate to help the implementation team scope infra and rollout. Two notes up front:

- These are estimates based on the sample traffic profile you shared (concurrent sessions ~120, typical prompt lengths 80–220 tokens, average generated tokens ~150).
- We recommended a short A/B window (3 weeks) to validate quality across 2 model families before committing to reserved capacity.

Attached: lumenix_loadshape_token_estimates_v1.xlsx (hourly profile + peak/day scenarios) and model_shortlist_rationale_v2.pdf (recs and tradeoffs).

High-level shortlist (why these):
- Redstone-13B-8k (quantized): great latency/cost for classification and short-response flows, conservative memory.
- Atlas-70B-32k (fp16): best for long-context summarization and multi-doc synthesis — heavier but better quality for long-case responses.
- Sparrow-7B (int8): fast and cheap for fallback / high-volume lightweight completions.

As next steps, can you confirm:
1) Which flows are highest priority for week-1 (search-augmentation, doc-summarization, chat)?
2) Any compliance constraints for token retention or KV caching?

Ben and Grace from our modeling/ops teams are looped for sizing and rollout planning. Happy to sync with your eng team Thursday if that works.

Thanks,
Priya
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: lumenix_loadshape_token_estimates_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
Attachment: model_shortlist_rationale_v2.pdf (document, 210KB)
From: Sara Holt <sara@lumenix.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Diego Ruiz <diego@lumenix.com>, eng-team@lumenix.com
Date: 2028-11-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumenix model shortlist & loadshape / token estimates — initial pass

Priya,

Thanks — the materials look useful and granular. Quick answers:

1) Week-1 priority: search-augmentation (users expect < 500ms median), then doc-summarization (batch backfill ok), chat assistant (low priority MVP).
2) Compliance: we cannot persist customer PII in long-term logs; short-term KV caching is fine for session affinity as long as we expire within 24 hours. Also need SOC2 evidence for data separation later in the procurement phase.

A couple clarifying Qs after skimming the spreadsheet:
- Your peak scenario assumes 12% conversion to long-summary flows — that seems high for us. Can we also see a 5% long-summary scenario?
- For Atlas-70B: do you have a recommended quantization or must it be fp16?

Happy to do a sync on Thursday 11/4 at 11:00 PT. If that works, please send a calendar invite.

—Sara
Head of Engineering, Lumenix
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Holt <sara@lumenix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-04T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumenix model shortlist & loadshape / token estimates — initial pass

Sara — thanks, Thursday 11:00 PT is confirmed (calendar invite sent). Quick replies inline and an updated ask for the implementation handoff: 

- We'll add a 5% long-summary column to the spreadsheet and re-run the peak/burst math; Ben will attach the updated sheet after the call.
- Atlas-70B: we recommend fp16 for best quality; quantized 4-bit runs are experimental for that model and require additional validation. For a production long-summary path we suggest fp16 on dedicated capacity for the initial rollout, with a later experiment to test 4-bit quant.

Handoff asks for your eng team before we move to dedicated sizing:
1) Confirm the three flows you want instrumented day-0 for quality/regression checks.
2) Provide a small sample of typical prompts for each flow (5–10 examples).
3) Any hard latency SLAs per flow (p50/p95).

Ben / Grace: after the call can you produce: (A) an updated token load sheet with 5% long-summary column, (B) a short ops plan mapping model -> capacity type (hosted vs dedicated) + estimated monthly cost bands. Mark anything that requires SOC2/compliance changes.

Thanks — see you Thursday.
Priya
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-06T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumenix model shortlist & loadshape / token estimates — internal sizing notes

Internal notes (posted after 11/4 sync):

- Updated sheet attached: lumenix_loadshape_token_estimates_v1.xlsx -> now includes a 5% long-summary column and a 1-in-24 hour spike scenario (attachment stub).
- Quick ops recs:
  * Week-0 (pilot, hosted): Sparrow-7B (int8) for high-volume search augmentation with prefix cache enabled; Redstone-13B-8k quantized on burst-capacity for mid-tier flows. Atlas-70B (fp16) on Dedicated for any long-summary requests we want high-fidelity on day-1.
  * Autoscaling knobs: scale by concurrent sessions and per-route token rate. Set burst headroom at 35% for the first 60 days.
  * Cost bands (monthly, approximate): Hosted pilot: $2.5k–$6k; Dedicated baseline (Atlas for long summaries): $18k–$28k depending on daily long-summary ratio.
- Compliance flag: Atlas on Dedicated will need private deployment review if Lumenix wants no cross-tenant KV persistence; add Monica to procurement thread for SOC2 evidence.

I'll attach the updated workbook to the hubspot deal and drop the short ops plan in the Drive link.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Holt <sara@lumenix.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-11-09T10:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lumenix model shortlist & loadshape / token estimates — handoff to implementation

Sara — thanks for the sync earlier this week. Finalizing the handoff notes below so your eng team can pick up implementation planning: 

Deliverables we left you with:
- Updated token/load sheet (5% long-summary column) — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_lumenix_onboarding (sheet named: lumenix_loadshape_token_estimates_v1.xlsx)
- Model shortlist & ops mapping (attached in Drive, model_shortlist_rationale_v2.pdf)
- Short ops plan (Ben): model -> capacity type + cost bands (link in Drive)

Day-0 instrumenting (agreed):
- Routes: search-augmentation (p50 target 400ms), doc-summarization batch (p95 target 2.5s), chat-assistant (best-effort).
- QA/telemetry: token-level latencies, per-route error rates, sample prompt set recordings.
- Retention policy: KV cache TTL 24 hours, short-term logs 7 days (PII scrubbed).

Next steps from Redwood:
1) Ben to upload ops plan + final workbook to the HubSpot deal (done).
2) Monica to start SOC2 evidence request for Atlas Dedicated (Monica, please kick off procurement items).
3) Schedule a 30-day check-in to review quality and cost vs estimates (suggest 12/11).

Sara — please confirm the contact on your side who will own the day-0 rollout (name + email) so we can set up invites and access. If there are any changes to the traffic assumptions please flag now — we can re-run the sizing quickly.

Thanks everyone — looping in Monica for the SOC2 procurement path.
Priya
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
